author: fester
body: The check no spirv-val on this box can do. It does not know SPIR-V semantics; it knows the shape a module must have: the five-word magic / version / bound / schema header, and an instruction stream that walks to the exact end, every header carrying a non-zero word count that does not run past the words that are there. A truncated instruction, a miscounted header, a lost operand -- the failures a hand-built or emitter-built word list actually produces -- do not survive this walk. Deeper (every id below the bound, types consistent) is the next rung; this is the floor.

author: fester
body: The text view, rendered FROM the words rather than from a second walk of the IR. This is what lets the text plug and the binary plug share one emitter: the plug emits words, and where a human-readable listing is wanted the words are disassembled here. Every operand is placed by the same per-opcode model the validator uses, so the text cannot drift from the binary -- it is the binary, spelled out. Ids are numbers (%7), which is what a module actually contains; the friendly type names the old emitter printed were a fiction it maintained separately.
